title: Cranial nerves anatomy
description: Twelve pairs leave the brain directly — smell to tongue movement — and they are examined in strict order in every neurological exam.

questions.question: How many cranial nerves are there?
questions.answer: There are 12 paired cranial nerves, numbered I through XII. Their functions include smell, vision, eye movement, facial sensation, hearing, swallowing and tongue movement.

questions.question: Which cranial nerve controls facial expression?
questions.answer: The facial nerve, cranial nerve VII, supplies most muscles of facial expression. The trigeminal nerve, cranial nerve V, carries most facial skin sensation.

questions.question: What is the olfactory nerve (CN I)?
questions.answer: Sensory filaments from nasal epithelium to bulb. Function: Smell.

questions.question: Where does the oculomotor nerve (CN III) originate?
questions.answer: Midbrain nerve to four eye muscles + lid + pupil. Function: Eye elevation/adduction, lid lift, pupil constriction.

questions.question: What does the trigeminal nerve (CN V) do?
questions.answer: Function: Face sensation + muscles of mastication. Three divisions: ophthalmic, maxillary, mandibular.
